title: Spontaneous Hawking Radiation from Dynamical Black-Hole Formation in Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Shunichiro Kinoshita, Keiju Murata, Daisuke Yamamoto, Ryosuke Yoshii
abstract: We show that Hawking radiation spontaneously generated by dynamical black-hole formation can be realized in a local quantum spin model. Starting from the ground state corresponding to the early-time vacuum, with no initially prepared excitations, we follow the dynamics induced by the evolving geometry. In the corresponding continuum quantum field theory, Hawking particle creation is associated with nontrivial Bogoliubov mixing between the in- and out-mode decompositions. We derive the resulting renormalized local energy density in the continuum quantum field theory, which corresponds to an energy-weighted integral of the Hawking spectrum, and identify its counterpart as a local spin observable whose expectation value quantitatively reproduces the continuum prediction, including its dependence on the surface gravity. The agreement persists over a finite time window whose duration grows logarithmically with system size, revealing the crossover from universal continuum Hawking physics to lattice-cutoff dynamics. These results establish a microscopic route to quantum simulation of quantum field theory in curved spacetime, connecting field-theoretic particle creation directly to experimentally accessible many-body observables.
summary: This work shows that spontaneous Hawking radiation, typically associated with curved spacetime, can be modeled using a local quantum spin system. By calculating the local energy density using spin observables, the authors successfully reproduce the continuum QFT prediction for Hawking radiation. This establishes a powerful, microscopic route for quantum simulation of quantum field theory in curved spacetime.
main_problem: To demonstrate a microscopic realization of spontaneous Hawking radiation generated by dynamical black-hole formation within a local quantum spin model.
main_result: The expectation value of a local spin observable quantitatively reproduces the continuum Quantum Field Theory prediction for the energy density associated with Hawking radiation.
method: The authors map the QFT problem onto a quantum spin system, calculating the renormalized local energy density using spin observables and comparing it to continuum predictions derived from Bogoliubov mixing.
model_or_system: The system is a local quantum spin model (e.g., related to Majorana fermions) simulating a 2D spacetime geometry evolving from flat to black-hole geometry. The dynamics are governed by a complex spin Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Renormalized local energy density ($ho_j(t)$), spatially averaged energy density ($ ar{ho}(t)$), and mode functions ($\phi^-_n,j$).
important_parameters: Surface gravity ($\kappa$), system size ($L$), and time window duration (which grows logarithmically with $L$).
main_assumptions: The agreement between the spin observable and the continuum prediction is limited to a finite time window, signaling the crossover to lattice-cutoff dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures show the time evolution of the spatially averaged energy density ($ ar{ho}(t)$) plateauing at the QFT prediction, and mode functions exhibiting exponential decay consistent with QFT predictions in the intermediate time regime.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical link between Hawking radiation and spin systems, calculates the energy density using local spin observables, and then numerically verifies the agreement with continuum QFT predictions while also analyzing the breakdown of the model at late times.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, experimentally accessible many-body observable (local spin expectation value) that directly simulates a fundamental process in quantum gravity (Hawking radiation), bridging condensed matter physics with high-energy theory.
